issues.title: Right-identity operand typo

failure_location.quote: The \textbf{identity tensor} $\tI \in \FFF^{m \xx m \xx n}$ under $\mm$ is such that $\tI \mm \tA = \tA , \tB \mm \tA = \tB$ for all $\tA , \tB$ of compatible sizes.

issues.failure_explanation: The old definition requires B star A=B for every compatible A and B. With A=0, bilinearity of the product gives B star 0=0, contradicting any nonzero B. The intended right-identity law is B star I=B.
issues.overall_effect: The literal identity definition is inconsistent, although the intended identity tensor and all subsequent notation are clear from the immediate context.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the second identity law by B star_M I = B, leaving I star_M A = A unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The terminology, product definition, and the zero-tensor test uniquely force the identity tensor as the second operand. This is a single transcriptional operand error and requires no change to any argument or guarantee.

issues.title: Circular real-closure characterization

failure_location.quote: The characterization of those complex transforms that induce real tubal rings is given bellow.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $V = (\RR^{1 \xx 1 \xx n},+,\mm)$ be a tubal ring

issues.failure_explanation: The prose advertises a characterization of complex transforms inducing real tubal rings, but the supporting lemma assumes that the real tube space is already a tubal ring, which already entails closure. This makes its local formulation circular as a selection criterion for arbitrary invertible transforms. Its exact citation, Lemma 2 of Demystifying Tubal Tensor Algebra, already supplies the intended characterization and proof; the issue is the restatement, not a substantial mathematical argument missing from the available justification.
issues.overall_effect: The locally stated lemma fails to express the advertised real-closure criterion for arbitrary invertible transforms. The intended criterion is supplied by the result already cited, and later results separately assuming a real tubal ring remain conditional.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Start with an arbitrary invertible complex matrix M and state that the induced product is closed on real tubes if and only if every row of M is real or has a complex-conjugate partner. Remove the premise that the real tube space is already a tubal ring and retain the existing exact citation proving this characterization. No new local proof is needed for this formulation repair.
issues.why_classification: Correctly restating the result already precisely cited is a short local repair preserving the intended characterization and subsequent conditional statements. The current circular wording is misleading, but the repair does not require the new nontrivial sufficiency argument assumed by the former moderate rationale.

issues.title: Unsupported minimal-generator cardinality inference

failure_location.quote: Showing that for all $j \in [r]$ there exists $k \in [r']$ such that $\bs{s}_{j,j} \mm \vec{\matW}_k^\CT \mm  \tU_{:,j} \neq \bs{0}$, hence $r' \geq r$.

issues.failure_explanation: A single candidate generator can have a nonzero pairing with several indexed singular vectors, so the displayed quantified statement alone does not imply r'>=r. The minimality claim can nevertheless be proved locally: since the r-th singular tube is nonzero, some transformed frontal slice has its r-th singular value nonzero; facewise ordering then gives that slice rank r. Projecting any module generating set to that slice yields a vector-space generating set of an r-dimensional range, forcing at least r generators.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma's spanning assertion is proved, but its minimality conclusion is not justified by the written inference. The later rank definitions do not require the specific invalid quantifier step.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the invalid counting inference with the following local argument. Since the r-th singular tube is nonzero, choose a transformed frontal slice k on which its entry is nonzero. Facewise singular-value ordering and vanishing of all later singular tubes give rank(X-hat(:,:,k)) = r. Evaluating any r'-element module generating set on slice k produces r' vectors spanning this r-dimensional matrix range, hence r' is at least r.
issues.why_classification: The minimality conclusion remains unchanged and follows from a short, routine projection-to-one-slice rank argument. This repairs a genuine inference but requires no new proof architecture, auxiliary lemma, or weakening.

issues.title: Missing transform-scale factor in the multirank error formula
issues.failure_explanation: If Z_hat=Z times_3(cQ), then ||Z_hat||_F^2=|c|^2||Z||_F^2. Matrix Eckart-Young gives the discarded transformed energy as the sum of the squared discarded transformed singular values, so the original-domain squared error equals |c|^{-2} times that sum. For example, with n=m=p=1 and M=2, the old right-hand side is four times the nonzero residual's squared original norm.
issues.overall_effect: Only the exact numerical error identity is misnormalized. The best-approximation inequality remains valid because the same positive scale applies to all compared residuals.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Write M = cQ with Q unitary and insert the uniquely required factor |c|^{-2} before the discarded transformed singular-value sum in the squared-error identity. Leave the best-approximation inequality unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The transform definition directly gives ||Z-hat||_F^2 = |c|^2||Z||_F^2, uniquely fixing the normalization. This is a transcriptional scale omission in the exact formula; it does not alter the approximation result or require any proof reconstruction.

issues.title: Missing lower bound for tubal-ring length
issues.failure_explanation: The argument proves length(R_n)<=ell by assigning at least one canonical component to each strict step. To obtain length(R_n)=ell, it must also prove length(R_n)>=ell. The canonical decomposition supplies this through the strict chain formed by successively adjoining the nonzero ideals generated by e_1,...,e_ell, but that direction is absent from the written proof.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted equality is only half proved. The missing direction is elementary and does not change the subsequent tubal-length framework once inserted.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: After proving the upper bound, define I_k = direct-sum_{j=1}^k <e_j> for k=1,...,ell. Because the canonical ideals are nonzero and form a direct sum, 0 is strictly contained in I_1, which is strictly contained in I_2, and so on up to I_ell = R_n. This chain gives length(R_n) at least ell and completes the equality.
issues.why_classification: Only one elementary direction of the proof is omitted. The canonical decomposition already supplies the required strict chain, so a short local insertion proves the original theorem with no loss or downstream change.

issues.title: Single-slice projection need not be real

failure_location.quote: where $\tens{H}_j = \wh{\tI}_m \xx_3 \vm{e}_j \vm{e}_j^\CT \xx_3 \matMi \in \RR_n^{m \xx m}$ is the projection onto the $j$-th frontal slice in the transformed domain.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the displayed projector onto one transformed frontal slice belongs to R_n^{m x m}. The old example and conjugate-slice lemma establish instead that a real tensor's transformed slices on a non-real row pair must occur together as complex conjugates. Thus a projector supported only at j is generally complex; it is real only for a self-conjugate real row or after grouping j with its conjugate partner.
issues.overall_effect: The geometric single-slice interpretation of a multirank component is invalid for complex transforms inducing real products. Paired-component arguments elsewhere can remain valid after replacing the projector by a conjugacy-orbit projector.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For each transformed-slice index j, let O(j) be {j} when the corresponding row is real and {j,j'} when j' is its conjugate partner. Replace the single-slice tensor by the orbit projector H_O(j) obtained from the transformed identity using the mask sum_{k in O(j)} e_k e_k^H and then applying M^{-1}. State that H_O(j) is real and projects onto the real conjugacy-orbit component; an individual-slice projector is generally only a complexified projector.
issues.why_classification: The repair is contained, but it must abandon the claimed independent real projection onto one slice throughout the natural complex-transform regime and replace it by a paired component. The resulting geometric statement is recognizably comparable, but this is a meaningful conceptual weakening rather than a no-loss routine edit.

issues.title: Non-real counterexample in the conjugate-pair necessity proof
issues.failure_explanation: For alpha=(1-i)/sqrt(2), the coefficient on slice s in A^(2) is conjugate(alpha). Reality requires the coefficient on its paired slice s' to be alpha, the conjugate of conjugate(alpha). The old construction instead uses -alpha. This violates the old paper's own conjugate-slice condition, so the construction cannot witness failure of an optimality statement quantified only over real tensors.
issues.overall_effect: The imaginary-part half of the intra-pair orthogonality lemma is not proved, leaving the complex-conjugate-row case of the necessity direction in the main characterization unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the definition of A-hat^(2), replace the term -alpha E_2 on slice s' by +alpha E_2. The two coefficients are then conjugate(alpha) and alpha, as required for a real tensor.
issues.why_classification: The paper's own conjugate-slice condition uniquely forces this sign, and the intended conjugate-pair construction retains the same amplitudes and rank. The erroneous literal sign is transcriptional and can be corrected without reworking the intended comparison.

issues.title: Reversed signs in the complex-pair norm expansion
issues.failure_explanation: Writing C=X+iY gives <C,conjugate(C)>_F=||X||_F^2-||Y||_F^2+2i<X,Y>_F under the paper's convention. Hence 2 Re(g<C,conjugate(C)>_F) contributes +2 Re(g)(||X||_F^2-||Y||_F^2)-4 Im(g)<X,Y>_F. The old displayed formula has -2 and +4 instead. Because the following choices of amplitudes are tailored to the reversed expression, merely correcting the display does not validate the two contradiction arguments.
issues.overall_effect: Both the real-part and imaginary-part arguments for orthogonality within a conjugate row pair fail, and therefore the corresponding part of the main necessity proof is unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Let C = A_j-B_j, S = g_{s,s}+g_{s',s'}, u = Re(g_{s',s}), and v = Im(g_{s',s}). Replace the expansion by S||C||_F^2 + 2u(||Re C||_F^2-||Im C||_F^2) - 4v<Re C,Im C>_F. Rebuild the two contradiction witnesses using the corrected quadratic: for u != 0 one may use A_j = diag(1, i sqrt((S-u)/(S-2u))); after establishing u=0, for v != 0 use A_j = diag(a(1-i),1+i)/sqrt(2) with a^2 = (S-2v)/(S+v), placing the conjugate matrix on the paired slice. Positivity of the corresponding two-by-two Gram block makes these choices valid, and comparison of the two rank-one truncations forces u=v=0, restoring the intra-pair lemma and the dependent necessity result.
issues.why_classification: Correcting the displayed signs alone leaves both tailored contradiction arguments invalid. The same proof architecture can be retained, but it requires nontrivial recalibration of two witnesses, positivity checks, and new case comparisons. This is a contained substantive repair preserving the theorem, hence moderate rather than minor or serious.

issues.title: False nonuniform tSVDMII compression ordering

failure_location.quote: Then for all $\tX \in \RR^{m \xx p \xx n}$ and $\gamma \in (0,1)$, we have $r_{\gamma} (\matM_0) \leq r_{\gamma} (\matM_1)$.

issues.failure_explanation: Take n=2, m=p=1, Q=I, D=diag(2,1), and a real tensor whose Q-transform entries are (1,1). Both Q and DQ satisfy the theorem's structural assumptions. At gamma=3/4, the squared singular values under Q are (1,1), so r_gamma(Q)=2, whereas under DQ they are (4,1), so r_gamma(DQ)=1. Thus the claimed inequality 2<=1 fails. The proof's identity between 1-beta and original-domain relative error is invalid because original-domain energy weights the transformed components by the inverse squared row scales. In addition, the displayed algorithm's stated input M=cW does not include a genuinely nonuniform DQ.
issues.overall_effect: The universal compression comparison and the associated prose claiming that nonuniform scaling is necessarily detrimental are unsupported. The main DQ characterization of fixed-multirank optimality is not affected by this root.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the ordering claim for the raw tSVDMII scores, for which no universal direction holds. For a compression comparison under M_1 = DQ, extend the energy-threshold routine using original-domain component energies: sort |d_k|^{-2}|s-tilde_{j,j,k}|^2 and normalize their cumulative sum by the sum of these weighted values. These quantities equal the corresponding squared singular values under Q, so the corrected component count satisfies r_gamma(DQ) = r_gamma(Q). Revise the prose to say that nonuniform scaling gives no advantage for Frobenius-energy compression, while the unweighted transformed-energy ordering is a feature-weighting heuristic and can move the count in either direction.
issues.why_classification: The counterexample rules out a sign reversal or other local correction to the stated raw-algorithm theorem, and the nonuniform case also lies outside the displayed algorithm's input contract. A contained weighted extension supplies a recognizably comparable universal compression statement, but it substantively changes the adaptive energy criterion and associated prose, so the issue exceeds minor without requiring global reconstruction or major loss.
